title: Non-invasive electromagnetic and infrared based observations for late-onset sepsis and apnea in preterm infants
summary:
Premature babies often experience breathing pauses (apneas), which can potentially be harmful to the children's further development. These breathing pauses are caused either by the brain's respiratory drive stopping ("central apnea") or by the child closing off the upper airway through muscular effort ("straining," "obstructive apnea"). Both can also occur together ("mixed apnea"). For this reason, the baby's breathing must be continuously monitored so that breathing pauses can be responded to, for example by means of non-invasive respiratory support.
Despite considerable advances in medical and technical care, sepsis remains one of the most serious conditions in newborns and premature infants and is one of the most common causes of death in neonatal intensive care units. This type of sepsis, which is acquired during the stay on the ward (late-onset sepsis), can be caused by organisms originating from the hospital environment or from relatives/staff. In the baby, the infection manifests itself through, among other things, rapid breathing (tachypnea), a faster heartbeat (tachycardia), fever, cold hands and feet with a simultaneously warm trunk (centralization). For this reason, temperature should be continuously measured at the feet and on the body.
Currently, breathing and temperature are monitored using numerous measuring devices attached to the baby's skin. This restricts the movement of (premature) babies, can damage their skin, and can pose a risk of infection. At present, there are no measurement systems that can measure breathing movement and body temperature contactlessly. In our study, we would like to test a measurement system that can measure both at the same time without contact. For this purpose, a sensor is attached to the child's bed that can measure breathing and body temperature.

interventions.name: Non-interventional observational study. Preterm infants receiving non-invasive respiratory support with frequent apneas, as well as preterm and term neonates at risk of infection, will be prospectively examined. criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- For the respiration study arm: preterm infants (GA 23+0 to 36+6/7 or with a birth weight <1500 g) as well as term infants with invasive or non-invasive respiratory support (CPAP or NIPPV); and for the sepsis study arm: preterm infants (GA 23+0 to 36+6/7 or with a birth weight <1500 g) as well as term infants with an increased likelihood of developing sepsis, e.g. due to the presence of central catheters or perinatal acidosis
- Clinically sufficiently stable general condition
- Written informed consent from the parents, provided after a detailed personal discussion and review of the parent information sheet
Exclusion criteria:
For the respiratory part
•	Severe congenital malformation of the thorax, abdomen, or internal organs
•	Chromosomal aberrations
•	Severe forms of pulmonary dysfunction (e.g. pulmonary edema, atelectasis, pneumothorax)
For the temperature part
•	Chromosomal aberrations
•	Syndromic disorders affecting temperature regulation
